title: decree message frontmatter
description: The YAML frontmatter of a decree message: a migration (.decree/migrations/*.md), an inbox message (.decree/inbox/*.md) or a cron file (.decree/cron/*.md). The body below the frontmatter is the task, in markdown; decree never changes it. A message has one of two shapes: a message that starts a run of a machine (`machine`, with `params`), or a reply to a run waiting in a `person` state (`to` and `event`). Any other key is kept as written and ignored by decree. `decree check` checks the rest (M1-M3): that the machine exists, that `params` fit its `data`, and that a cron expression parses. Reference: docs/reference/messages.md.

id.description: Names the run folder, runs/<id>/. decree sets it at claim if missing: YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ-xxxxxx, the UTC time plus 6 lowercase hex chars. A migration's id is its file stem.

machine.description: The machine that runs this message: the name of .decree/machines/<name>.yml (M1-M3). Required on every message that is not a reply.

state.description: Written by decree only: a mirror of the run's current state, in runs/<id>/message.md. Authors never set it; the run's events.jsonl is the record.

parent.description: Written by `decree emit` and decree: the id of the run that emitted this message, or that invoked this child run.

depth.description: Written by `decree emit`: the parent's depth plus 1. Absent means 0. `decree emit` refuses a depth above 10.

trigger.description: Written by decree: how the run started. `migration`, `cron`, `emit`, `inbox`, or `invoke` (a child run). Scripts read it as DECREE_TRIGGER.

params.description: Sets the machine's `data` for this run, overriding the defaults, like SCXML <invoke><param>. Each name must be a `data` entry of the machine, with a value of its type, and one of its `enum` values if it has one (M1-M3).

traceparent.description: W3C Trace Context: the span this message's run continues, 00-<trace id>-<parent span id>-<flags>. The run takes its trace id and its run span's parent from it; an invalid one is ignored and the run starts a new trace. Written by decree for child runs and by `decree emit` from TRACEPARENT; any tool may set it, such as a webhook relaying an upstream trace (docs/reference/observability.md, Traces).

tracestate.description: W3C Trace Context: vendor data passed on unchanged beside a valid `traceparent`, to every script as TRACESTATE and to child runs and emitted messages. Ignored without a valid `traceparent`.

to.description: Makes this message a reply, not a new run: the wait id (<run id>.w<seq>) of a run paused in a `person` state, or the run id meaning its current wait. `decree event` writes replies.

event.description: In a reply: the event to deliver, one of the waiting state's options.

cron.description: In a cron file (.decree/cron/*.md) only: a standard cron expression. On each `decree daemon` pass, a due cron file is queued as a message with its other keys and its body (M3).

oneOf.title: message
oneOf.description: A message that starts a run of a machine: `machine`, and no `to`.

oneOf.title: reply
oneOf.description: A reply to a run waiting in a `person` state: `to` and `event`. The body is an optional note for the run's later scripts.
